whatChanged: NEW: Curium agrees to merge with Lantheus at $102.50 a share in cash plus CVRs worth up to $12.00, a total transaction value of up to ~$8.0bn, combining two of the largest radiopharmaceutical businesses (lnth-curium-acquisition)

ADVANCED: Prologis and Segro agree terms of a firm Rule 2.7 recommended acquisition -- 0.0920 new Prologis shares per Segro share, valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn with a GBP3.5bn partial cash alternative (pld-sgro-takeover-bid) (rumored -> confirmed)

ADVANCED: KKR signs a definitive agreement to acquire Integer Holdings for $127 a share in cash, an enterprise value of ~$5.7bn, unanimously recommended by the board (itgr-kkr-takeover) (rumored -> confirmed)

themes.label: UK-listed franchises broken up or taken private
themes.note: London-listed names remain a magnet for control-changing bids from overseas and private capital, and one has now gone firm: Prologis and Segro have agreed terms of a recommended Rule 2.7 acquisition valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn, which would remove one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs from the LSE (pld-sgro-takeover-bid), both easyJet suitors must declare a firm offer or walk away by August 7 with the board already agreed in principle to Apollo's ~GBP5.7bn terms (ezj-apollo-takeover), and CD&R-owned OCS Group's agreed GBP3.1bn takeover of facilities-management leader Mitie will delist another name entirely (ocs-mitie-acquisition).

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: PE-, sovereign- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names private, and two more firmed up this week: KKR signed a definitive $127-a-share, ~$5.7bn agreement for Integer Holdings (itgr-kkr-takeover) days after EA left the Nasdaq at $210 a share in the $55bn PIF-Silver Lake-Affinity take-private (ea-pif-consortium-take-private). Still live: Apollo and Castlelake both face an August 7 deadline on easyJet (ezj-apollo-takeover), Pacific Equity Partners' SG Fleet vehicle bids A$3.60 a share for FleetPartners (fpr-sgfleet-takeover-bid), Grant Thornton and New Mountain Capital's $5bn all-cash deal for CBIZ runs a go-shop to August 27 (cbz-grant-thornton-acquisition), Steel Partners' $16.75-a-share bid for InMode is fought through both the Haifa court and the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), EQT keeps raising for Perpetual (ppt-eqt-takeover-bid), Frasers Group's EUR38-a-share tender for Hugo Boss is unconditional (boss-frasers-takeover-offer), Stripe and Advent's $53bn offer for PayPal remains live after board rejection (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid), and Sazerac's revived ~$15bn approach for Brown-Forman has been rejected as not actionable (bfb-sazerac-takeover-bid).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital and commercial commitments keep pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the guided numbers keep going up: Amazon's 2026 capex guide raised to ~$220bn with capacity constrained into 2027 (amzn-capex-raise-2026) and Alphabet's raised to as much as $205bn (googl-capex-raise-2026), Nvidia's talks to backstop ~$250bn of financing for OpenAI's 10GW Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop) and its equity-plus-Vera-Rubin-capacity pact with Safe Superintelligence (nvda-ssi-partnership), the $10bn Naver AI factory scaling to 200MW with Brookfield capital (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), Orange and Morrison's EUR3bn, 400MW French data-centre JV (ora-morrison-datacenter-jv), Microsoft's at-scale deployment of AMD's Helios systems (msft-amd-helios-partnership), NVIDIA's $1.5bn prepaid packaging capacity at Amkor (amkr-nvidia-packaging-partnership), Verizon's $1bn dark-fiber deal with Google (vz-google-fiber-partnership), Samsung Electronics' ~$200bn memory and foundry MOU with Broadcom (samsungelec-avgo-chip-partnership), SK hynix's long-term HBM pact with NVIDIA behind a 2GW Vera Rubin AI factory (skhynix-nvda-ai-partnership), Everus's $295m purchase of modular mechanical and electrical specialist Epsilon Industries (ecg-epsilon-acquisition), Doosan buying control of Korea's sole wafer maker SK Siltron for KRW2.3trn (doosan-sksiltron-acquisition), and Prysmian paying ~$3.8bn for Atkore's conduit and cable-management business to sell into the same North American build-out (atkr-prysmian-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing is now the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and it concentrates credit and equity risk on the supplier's balance sheet: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee ~$250bn of lease and debt financing for OpenAI's Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), took a reported ~$5bn equity stake in pre-revenue Safe Superintelligence alongside a compute commitment (nvda-ssi-partnership), and is buying ~4.5% of Naver via a ~$1bn share issue tied to a 200MW AI factory (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), while AMD is investing up to $5bn in Anthropic against a tens-of-billions MI450 purchase commitment (amd-anthropic-chip-partnership).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep drawing legal fire: the signed, DOJ-cleared Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger is formally paused by court stipulation until five days after an antitrust trial or June 1, 2027, with Paramount owing ~$7m a day if the pause runs past September 30, 2026 (psky-wbd-acquisition), while InMode's special committee remains procedurally frozen pending the Haifa court's ruling on the competing buyout bids, with the fight now also running through the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout).
